findings.note: The required regression check is recorded passes:true, but the very log it cites concludes the opposite in its own words: 'passes is therefore recorded false. Full-repository regression does not pass on this branch.' The completed 2026-08-21 full run lists three failing suites, one of which (tests/repository-release-validation.tests.sh) the log itself classifies as a REAL FAILURE, not designed-red, and whose stated cause names this feature directly ('epic-194-a6-lite-integration: stage-provenance: spec top-level contract hashes are stale', masking a still-unresolved 'task plan hash is stale'). The implementation report independently reproduces the same task-plan-hash failure. A required check asserted green over evidence that states it is red is a misrepresented verification result, not a scoping decision.

The defense-in-depth check is faked verification. design.md Test Strategy item 6 and tasks.md Done-When both require a companion fixture that proves the ship-time recheck 'still independently Blocks' a component the intake-time evaluation did not flag, explicitly 'a tested, not merely documented, property'. What is implemented is a grep of the live plugins/sdd-ship/skills/ship/SKILL.md for the substring 'check-risk-upgrade': no fixture is constructed, no gate is invoked, no exit code or Block message is observed. T-003.red.log confirms this assertion passed in RED as well (1 passed / 13 failed), so it has zero discriminating power for this task, yet it is counted as 1 of the 14 green and the implementation report records 'Defense-in-depth confirmed: satisfied'. This is the security-relevant second stage of a two-stage access-control-like gate and it is untested.

findings.ref: acceptance-tests.md AC-019 vs tests/lite-spec-capability-block.tests.sh TEST-019-static-g / TEST-019-functional-a..c
findings.note: AC-019 requires the Block to be verified for (i) non-overridability -- '--lite never overrides', (ii) occurrence 'before any specs/<feature>/ file exists', and (iii) parity 'as an existing keyword-match fixture'. None of the three is exercised. No test ever passes --lite; static-g greps only the fragment 'regardless of whether the', which names neither --lite nor any override; no test asserts the absence of a created specs/<feature>/ artifact; and no keyword-match fixture is run anywhere in the suite, so the functional-a/b labels ('same exit code as an existing keyword-match fixture', 'same shape as a keyword-match Block') assert a comparison the suite never performs -- the assertions behind them are a hard-coded 'exit == 10' and a 'full-required:' prefix test.

findings.note: The artifact this task actually implements is absent from the bundle. findings.ref: acceptance-tests.md AC-021 / AC-010; tasks.md T-003 Done-When 'Single-file, human-copy-only'

placeholder-scan is recorded passes:true while its cited log ends 'Placeholder scan FAILED (5 finding(s)) ... exit: 1' against CHANGELOG.md -- a file T-003 declares as its own output and modified this session. The scanner's own message states each finding 'must be implemented properly, or explicitly accepted by a human in the quality-gate report'; no such human acceptance appears anywhere in the bundle, only the contract author's own prose disclosure. Pre-existence at merge-base bd48ce8c is well proven, but pre-existence is not the exemption the tool defines.

findings.ref: tasks.md T-003 Planned Files; traceability.md T-003 row -- tests/fixtures/epic-194-lite-spec/
findings.note: The declared fixture tree tests/fixtures/epic-194-lite-spec/ was never created; both suites build their fixtures inline via mktemp/heredoc. A planned and traceability-declared output is silently missing, and that traceability row's evidence paths (verification/T-003/green-sh.log, .../red-sh.log) also do not match the files that actually exist (T-003.green.log, T-003.red.log, qg/T-003/unit-acceptance-green.log).

The twins model the Registry differently: the .sh fixture nests eligibility as lite_policy.{eligible,upgrade_reasons}, matching design.md's Data Plan, while the .ps1 fixture flattens eligible/upgrade_reasons onto the capability object. The PowerShell half therefore never exercises the designed Registry shape, so the twin pair is not the runtime-equivalence check it is presented as.

The .sh suite hard-depends on an unguarded python3 to assemble the fragment. On a runner without python3 the suite aborts mid-run under set -e, printing neither a FAIL line nor the trailing 'Results:' summary -- an opaque failure mode at odds with the tasks.md CI-resilience constraint. A capability probe with a visible skip, or jq/awk assembly, would keep the tally honest.
